_readme: OPTIONAL overrides for the weekly BYOK live tier.
You probably do NOT need this file. Every brand's credential now comes from a
named repo secret: the seven that predate this tier (BYOK_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY,
BYOK_MOONSHOT_API_KEY, BYOK_ZHIPU_API_KEY, BYOK_GOOGLE_API_KEY,
BYOK_OPENAI_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY, VERTEX_SA_JSON) plus four that follow the
convention a brand derives, `BYOK_<BRAND>_API_KEY`:
BYOK_OPEN_ROUTER_API_KEY      (also covers open_router_glm / _qwen /
_nemotron / _mimo / _grok)
BYOK_DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
BYOK_FIREWORKS_API_KEY
BYOK_AMAZON_BEDROCK_API_KEY   (the bearer token; bedrock_grok inherits it)
That covers 25 of the 26 rows. A new brand needs no entry here and no code
change — create `BYOK_<BRAND>_API_KEY` and pass it in contract-tests.yml.
WHAT THIS FILE IS STILL FOR
A credential that is not one string, or a slot field that is not a key.
Set the repo secret BYOK_LIVE_KEYS to this JSON; any field here wins over
the default written in the test row.
1. cp byok-live-keys.example.json byok-live-keys.json   (the copy is gitignored)
2. keep only what you are overriding, delete the rest
3. pnpm run byok:live:check    — what it would cover, spending nothing
pnpm run byok:live          — the real calls
A value still holding a placeholder ('…' or angle brackets) counts as ABSENT,
so a half-filled file is a valid file.
_notes: azure is the ONLY row with no named secret, and it is deliberate: ZERO
production slots use the `azure` provider — both real Azure configs arrive as
openai_compatible at /openai/v1/, a path pinned offline from Microsoft's own
docs. Fill this only if you happen to have a deployment.
Bedrock with SigV4 instead of a bearer token (the builder takes either):
Either form needs the model enabled under Bedrock Model access in that
region, or the call returns AccessDeniedException.
A different MODEL for a row, which is how a newer generation gets tested
-fable) may all hold the SAME key — they are six generations with mutually
exclusive request shapes, not six accounts.
